name: Space Syntax Theory
citation: Hillier, B. & Hanson, J. (1984). The social logic of space. Cambridge University Press.

constructs.description: Syntactic integration predicts pedestrian movement flows (R² = 0.50-0.80). Grid cell metric coding and hippocampal cognitive maps route through well-connected nodes.
Spatial coherence predicts navigation success. Low spatial PE → confident mapping → reduced navigational stress.
Visible area and compactness predict perceived spaciousness, surveillance, and comfort. Affordance richness from syntactic structure.
Goal-state override: purposeful shoppers with specific destinations override natural movement patterns. Expertise effects and cultural-semantic overlay.

irreducible_residual.narrative: Irreducible residual ~35%: sociological logic by which spatial configuration encodes social structure across time (~20%), topological-versus-metric debate (~5%), and cultural variation in integration-movement correlations (~10%). These reflect the sociological dimension of Space Syntax that sits outside the neural-mechanistic framework.
